pairs.fullEnglish: Yaakov went out from the well of Sheva and went to Charan.
He came upon the place and spent the night there, because the sun had set. He took some of the stones of the place, placed them at his head, and lay down in that place.
He dreamed, and behold, a ladder was planted in the earth, and its top reached to the height of heaven; and behold, the angels of יְיָ were ascending and descending on it.

And behold, the glory of יְיָ stood over him, and He said, ‘I am יְיָ, the God of Avraham your father and the God of Yitzchak. The land on which you are lying I will give to you and to your descendants.’

‘Your descendants will be numerous as the dust of the earth, and you will become strong to the west, to the east, to the north, and to the south. All the families of the earth will be blessed on your account and on account of your descendants.’

‘Behold, My Word will be your support, and I will guard you in every place to which you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you.’
Yaakov awoke from his sleep and said, ‘Truly, the glory of יְיָ dwells in this place, and I did not know.’
He was afraid and said, ‘How awe-inspiring is this place! This is no ordinary place, but a place in which there is favor from before יְיָ; and this is a gate facing heaven.’
Yaakov rose early in the morning, took the stone that he had placed at his head, set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
He called the name of that place Bais El; however, the name of the city had formerly been Luz.
Yaakov made a vow, saying, ‘If the Word of יְיָ will be my support, and He will guard me on this road on which I am going, and give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,’
‘This stone which I have set up as a pillar will be one upon which I shall worship before יְיָ; and of everything You give me, I will set apart one in ten before You.’
Yaakov lifted his feet and went to the land of the people of the east.

He saw, and behold, there was a well in the field, and behold, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, because from that well they watered the flocks; and a large stone was over the mouth of the well.
All the flocks would gather there, and they would roll the stone from over the mouth of the well, water the sheep, and return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.
Yaakov said to them, ‘My brothers, where are you from?’ They said, ‘We are from Charan.’
He said to them, ‘Do you know Lavan son of Nachor?’ They said, ‘We know him.’
He said to them, ‘Is he well?’ They said, ‘He is well; and behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.’
He said, ‘Behold, there is still much of the day left; it is not the time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep, and go and pasture them.’
They said, ‘We cannot, until all the flocks gather and they roll the stone from over the mouth of the well; then we will water the sheep.’
While he was speaking with them, Rachel came with the sheep that belonged to her father, for she was a shepherdess.

When Yaakov saw Rachel, the daughter of Lavan, his mother's brother, and the sheep of Lavan, his mother's brother, Yaakov approached, rolled the stone from over the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Lavan, his mother's brother.
Yaakov kissed Rachel, raised his voice, and wept.
Lavan said to him, ‘Indeed, you are my kinsman and my flesh.’ He stayed with him for a month of days.
Lavan said to Yaakov, ‘Because you are my kinsman, should you serve me for nothing? Tell me what your wages shall be.’
Lavan had two daughters: the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
Leah's eyes were beautiful, and Rachel was beautiful in form and lovely in appearance.
Yaakov loved Rachel and said, ‘I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.’
Lavan said, ‘It is better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man. Stay with me.’
Yaakov served seven years for Rachel, and they were in his eyes like a few days, because he loved her.
Yaakov said to Lavan, ‘Give me my wife, for I have completed the days of my service, so that I may go in to her.’
Lavan gathered all the men of the place and made a feast.
When evening came, he took Leah his daughter and brought her in to him, and he went in to her.
Lavan gave her Zilpah his maidservant, to Leah his daughter as a maidservant.
When morning came, behold, she was Leah! He said to Lavan, ‘What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why have you deceived me?’
Lavan said, ‘It is not done this way in our place, to give the younger before the older.’
‘Complete the week of this one, and we will give you this one also, in return for the service that you will perform with me for another seven years.’
Yaakov did so and completed the week of this one, and he gave him Rachel his daughter as his wife.
Lavan gave Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maidservant as her maidservant.
He went in to Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him for another seven years.
יְיָ saw that Leah was hated and granted her conception, while Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuven, for she said, ‘For my affliction is revealed before יְיָ; for now my husband will love me.’
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, ‘For it has been heard before יְיָ that I am hated, and He has given me this one also.’ She called his name Shimon.
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, ‘This time my husband will become joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.’ Therefore he called his name Levi.
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, ‘This time I will give thanks before יְיָ.’ Therefore she called his name Yehudah, and she ceased bearing children.
Rachel saw that she had not borne children to Yaakov, and Rachel was jealous of her sister. She said to Yaakov, ‘Give me children; and if not, I am dead.’
Yaakov's anger grew strong against Rachel, and he said, ‘Behold, you are asking of me! Should you not ask from before יְיָ, who has withheld offspring of the womb from you?’
She said, ‘Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Go in to her, and she will bear children, and I will raise them, and I too will be built up through her.’
She gave him Bilhah her maidservant as a wife, and Yaakov went in to her.
Bilhah conceived and bore Yaakov a son.
Rachel said, ‘יְיָ has judged my case, and has also accepted my prayer and given me a son.’ Therefore she called his name Dan.
Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again and bore Yaakov a second son.
Rachel said, ‘יְיָ has accepted my petition through my supplication in my prayer. I desired to have a child like my sister, and one has indeed been given to me.’ She called his name Naftali.
Leah saw that she had ceased bearing children, and she took Zilpah her maidservant and gave her to Yaakov as a wife.
Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore Yaakov a son.
Leah said, ‘Good fortune has come!’ She called his name Gad.
Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore Yaakov a second son.
Leah said, ‘Praise has come to me, for now the women will praise me.’ She called his name Asher.
Reuven went out in the days of the wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to Leah his mother. Rachel said to Leah, ‘Now give me some of your son's mandrakes.’

She said to her, ‘Is it a small thing that you have taken my husband, that you would also take my son's mandrakes?’ Rachel said, ‘Then he shall lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes.’
Yaakov came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, ‘You shall come in to me, for I have indeed hired you with my son's mandrakes.’ He lay with her that night.
יְיָ accepted Leah's prayer, and she conceived and bore Yaakov a fifth son.
Leah said, ‘יְיָ has given my reward because I gave my maidservant to my husband.’ She called his name Yissachar.
Leah conceived again and bore Yaakov a sixth son.
Leah said, ‘יְיָ has given him to me as a good portion. This time my husband's dwelling will be with me, for I have borne him six sons.’ She called his name Zevulun.
Afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah.
Rachel's remembrance came before יְיָ, and יְיָ accepted her prayer and granted her conception.
She conceived and bore a son, and said, ‘יְיָ has gathered away my disgrace.’
She called his name Yosef, saying, ‘May יְיָ add another son for me.’
When Rachel had borne Yosef, Yaakov said to Lavan, ‘Send me away, so that I may go to my place and to my land.’
‘Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know the service with which I have served you.’
Lavan said to him, ‘If now I have found favor before you—I have learned by experience that יְיָ has blessed me on your account.’
He said, ‘Specify your wages to be paid by me, and I will give them.’
He said to him, ‘You know how I have served you, and how your livestock have fared with me.’
‘For the little that you had before me has grown exceedingly numerous, and יְיָ has blessed you on my account. But now, when shall I also provide for my own household?’
Lavan said, ‘Indeed, would that it be according to your word!’
He heard the words of Lavan's sons, who were saying, ‘Yaakov has taken everything that belonged to our father, and from what belonged to our father he has acquired all this property.’
Yaakov saw the expression on Lavan's face, and behold, it was not toward him as it had been yesterday and before that.
יְיָ said to Yaakov, ‘Return to the land of your fathers and to your birthplace, and My Word will be your support.’
He said to them, ‘I see the expression on your father's face, that it is not toward me as it was yesterday and before that; but the God of my father has been my support.’
‘You yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength.’
‘Your father deceived me and changed my wages ten times, but יְיָ did not allow him to do me harm.’
‘יְיָ separated your father's livestock and gave them to me.’
‘The angel of יְיָ said to me in the dream, “Yaakov!” And I said, “Here I am.”’
‘“I am God, who revealed Myself to you at Bais El, where you anointed a pillar and where you made a vow before Me. Now arise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.”’
Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, ‘Do we still have, now, a portion and an inheritance in our father's house?’
‘Are we not considered strangers by him? For he has sold us, and has indeed consumed our money.’
‘For all the wealth that יְיָ has separated from our father belongs to us and to our children. Now do everything that יְיָ has told you.’
Yaakov arose and lifted his children and his wives onto the camels.

He led away all his livestock and all his possessions that he had acquired, the livestock of his acquisition that he had acquired in Paddan Aram, to come to Yitzchak his father, to the land of Canaan.
Yaakov concealed it from the mind of Lavan the Aramean, in that he did not tell him that he was leaving.
He went away, he and all that belonged to him; he arose, crossed the Euphrates, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilad.
On the third day Lavan was told that Yaakov had gone away.
He took his kinsmen with him and pursued him for a seven-day journey, and caught up with him at the mountain of Gilad.
Lavan caught up with Yaakov. Yaakov had spread his tent on the mountain, and Lavan encamped his kinsmen on the mountain of Gilad.
Lavan said to Yaakov, ‘What have you done, concealing it from me and leading away my daughters like captives of the sword?’
‘Why did you hide yourself to leave, conceal it from me, and not tell me? I would have sent you away with joy and with songs of praise, with drums and with lyres.’
‘You did not let me kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.’
‘There is power in my hand to do you harm, but the God of your father said to me last night, “Take care not to speak with Yaakov from good to bad.”’
‘And now you have indeed gone away because you greatly longed for your father's house; but why have you taken the object of my worship?’
Yaakov answered and said to Lavan, ‘Because I was afraid, for I said, “Lest you take your daughters away from me by force.”’
Lavan entered Yaakov's tent and Leah's tent and the tent of the two concubines, but did not find it. He went out from Leah's tent and entered Rachel's tent.
Rachel had taken the images, put them in the camel's saddle, and sat upon them. Lavan felt through the entire tent, but did not find them.
She said to her father, ‘Let it not be grievous in my lord's eyes that I cannot rise before you, for the way of women is upon me.’ He searched, but did not find the images.
Yaakov grew angry and contended with Lavan. Yaakov answered and said to Lavan, ‘What is my guilt? What is my offense, that you have pursued me?’
‘Now that you have felt through all my belongings, what have you found of all the belongings of your house? Put it here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, and let them decide between the two of us.’
‘These twenty years I have been with you: your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried, and I have not eaten the rams of your flock.’
‘I did not bring you an animal torn by beasts. Whatever was missing from the count, you demanded from me. I kept watch by day, and I kept watch by night.’
‘By day the heat consumed me, and frost descended upon me at night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.’
‘Now come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and let it be a witness between me and you.’
Yaakov took a stone and raised it as a pillar.
Yaakov said to his kinsmen, ‘Gather stones.’ They took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.
Lavan called it יְגַר שַׂהֲדוּתָא, and Yaakov called it גַּלְעֵד.
Lavan said, ‘This heap is a witness between me and you today.’ Therefore he called its name גַּלְעֵד.
And the lookout, because he said, ‘May the Word of יְיָ watch between me and you, when we are hidden from one another.’
Lavan said to Yaakov, ‘Behold this heap, and behold the pillar that I have set up between me and you.’
‘May the God of Avraham and the god of Nachor judge between us, the god of their father.’ Yaakov swore by the One whom his father Yitzchak feared.
Lavan rose early in the morning, kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Lavan went away and returned to his place.
Yaakov went on his way, and the angels of יְיָ met him.
When Yaakov saw them, he said, ‘This is a camp from before יְיָ.’ He called the name of that place מַחֲנָיִם.
‘and I return in peace to my father's house, and the Word of יְיָ will be God to me.’

qualifications.he: הפסוק ממשיך את הנדר הפותח ב׳אִם׳ בפסוק הקודם. נשמר החיבור ׳וִיהֵא׳ בלי להוסיף ׳אז׳; הנוסח המצוטט אינו מסמן במפורש אם כאן מסתיים התנאי ומתחילה תוצאתו.
qualifications.en: This verse continues the vow opened by ‘if’ in the preceding verse. The connective ‘and will be’ is retained without adding ‘then’; the quoted wording does not explicitly mark whether the condition ends and its consequence begins at this point.

pairs.fullEnglish: When Lavan heard the news of Yaakov, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, embraced him, kissed him, and brought him into his house; and Yaakov related all these matters to Lavan.
He said, ‘What shall I give you?’ Yaakov said, ‘Do not give me anything. If you do this thing for me, I will again pasture your flock and guard it.’

‘I will pass through all your flock today. Remove from there every lamb that is spotted or patched, every dark lamb among the lambs, and every goat that is patched or spotted; and these shall be my wages.’

qualifications.he: ׳הסר׳ באנגלית מתרגם את הקריאה הראשית הַעֲדֵי. המקור מציג גם את החלופה אַעְדִּי. החלופה נשמרת כאן כפי שסופקה, בלי להכריע בפירושה הדקדוקי או להחליף בה בשתיקה את הקריאה הראשית.
qualifications.en: ‘Remove’ translates the main reading הַעֲדֵי. The supplied original also presents the alternative אַעְדִּי. That alternative is retained here as supplied, without adjudicating its grammatical interpretation or silently substituting it for the main reading.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘My righteousness will testify for me on a future day, when it comes before you concerning my wages: any goat with me that is neither spotted nor patched, and any lamb with me that is not dark, is stolen.’

That day he removed the male goats that were leg-marked or patched and all the female goats that were spotted or patched, everything that had white on it, and everything dark among the lambs, and gave them into the hands of his sons.
He put a three-day journey between himself and Yaakov, while Yaakov pastured Lavan's remaining flock.
He planted the rods that he had peeled in the channels, the place of the watering troughs, where the flock came to drink, facing the flock; and the animals mated when they came to drink.
The flock mated by the rods, and the flock bore young that were leg-marked, spotted, and patched.

Yaakov separated the lambs and put at the head of the flock all that were leg-marked and all that were dark in Lavan's flock. He made flocks for himself separately and did not mix them with Lavan's flock.
Whenever the early-bearing animals of the flock mated, Yaakov would put the rods before the eyes of the flock in the channels, so that the animals would mate by the rods.
But with the late-bearing animals of the flock he would not put the rods there. The late-born belonged to Lavan, and the early-born to Yaakov.
The man became exceedingly, exceedingly prosperous, and he had large flocks, maidservants and menservants, camels and donkeys.
Yaakov sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flock.
‘If he would say, “The spotted shall be your wages,” then the entire flock bore spotted young. And if he would say, “The leg-marked shall be your wages,” then the entire flock bore leg-marked young.’
‘At the time when the flock was mating, I lifted my eyes and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats mounting the animals of the flock were leg-marked, spotted, and white-marked.’
‘He said, “Now lift your eyes and see: all the male goats mounting the animals of the flock are leg-marked, spotted, and white-marked; for all that Lavan is doing to you is revealed before Me.”’
Lavan had gone to shear his flock, and Rachel concealed the images that belonged to her father.
A Word from before יְיָ came to Lavan the Aramean in a dream of the night and said to him, ‘Take care, lest you speak with Yaakov from good to bad.’
‘These twenty years I have been in your house: I served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times.’

‘Had the God of my father, the God of Avraham and the One whom Yitzchak fears, not been my support, you would surely now have sent me away empty-handed. My hardship and the weariness of my hands are revealed before יְיָ, and He issued a rebuke last night.’

Lavan answered and said to Yaakov, ‘The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, and the flock is my flock; and everything you see belongs to me. But as for my daughters, what can I do to these today, or to their children whom they have borne?’
‘If you afflict my daughters, and if you take wives in addition to my daughters—there is no one with us; see, the Word of יְיָ is a witness between me and you.’

qualifications.he: שתי אזהרות התנאי נשמרות: עינוי בנותיו ולקיחת נשים נוספות עליהן. החיבור ׳ואם׳ אינו מתורגם כדרישה ששני המעשים יתרחשו יחד כדי שתהא משמעות לעדות; מימר ה׳ הוא העד גם כשאין אדם עמם.
qualifications.en: The two conditional warnings are retained: afflicting his daughters and taking additional wives besides them. ‘And if’ is not a requirement that both acts occur together before the witness matters; the Word of יְיָ is the witness even when no human is with them.
qualifications.anchor: אִם תְּעַנֵּי יָת בְּנָתַי וְאִם תִּסַּב נְשִׁין עַל בְּנָתַי

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘This heap is a witness, and the pillar is a witness: I shall not cross beyond this heap to you for harm, and you shall not cross beyond this heap and this pillar to me for harm.’
Yaakov carried out a slaughter on the mountain and called his kinsmen to eat bread. They ate bread and spent the night on the mountain.

‘The one with whom you find the object of your worship shall not remain alive. Before our kinsmen, identify for yourself what of yours is with me, and take it for yourself.’ Yaakov did not know that Rachel had taken them.

qualifications.he: ׳מי שתמצא אצלו׳ משקף את הקריאה הראשית עִם. החלופה שבמקור היא אֲתַר, ׳מקום׳. הקשר התחבירי של ׳מקום׳ אל ׳לָא יִתְקַיַּם׳ אינו מוכרע כאן; אין להמיר את החלופה בנוסח על אדם. גוף התרגום משקף את הקריאה הראשית בלבד.
qualifications.en: ‘The one with whom you find’ reflects the main reading עִם. The supplied alternative is אֲתַר, ‘place.’ The syntactic relationship of ‘place’ to לָא יִתְקַיַּם remains unresolved here; that alternative is not converted into a statement about a person. The body renders the main reading only.
qualifications.anchor: דִּי תַשְׁכַּח יָת דַּחַלְתָּךְ לָא יִתְקַיַּם

pairs.fullEnglish: My people are divided about returning to My ways. They will encounter grievous affliction; together they will not walk with upright bearing.

How can I hand you over, Ephraim, or make an end of you, Israel? How can I scatter you as Admah, or make you like Zeboiim? The word of My covenant comes to meet Me; My mercies have all been stirred together.
They will follow the worship of ייָ. His Word is like a lion that roars; for He will roar, and the exiles will be gathered from the west.
Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood;
a heart that devises evil thoughts, and feet that hurry to run toward evil;
a false witness who speaks lies, and one who sets quarrels between brothers.
My son, guard your father's commandment, and do not stray from your mother's teaching.
Bind them continually within your heart, and wrap them around your neck.
The house of Israel is like one who sowed wind and reaped a whirlwind. Every day they multiply lies and plunder; they have established a covenant with the Assyrian, and they carry tribute to Egypt.
There is a case before יְיָ against those of the house of Judah, and He will deal with Jacob according to his ways; He repays him according to his upright deeds.
The prophet said to them: Was it not said of Jacob, before he was born, that he would become greater than his brother? And in his strength he contended in might with an angel.
For the commandment is a lamp, and teaching is light; and the way of life is both reproof and discipline.
They are to guard you from an evil woman and from the smoothness of a foreign woman's tongue.
Do not covet her beauty in your heart, and do not let her ensnare you with her eyebrows.
The prophet said to them: He is יְיָ, God of hosts, who revealed Himself to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and, as was said through Moses, His memorial is for every generation.
And you, be steadfast in the worship of your God. Keep kindness and justice, and continually hope for your God's deliverance.
Do not be like merchants who hold deceitful balances in their hands and love to rob.
And I am יְיָ your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. I will again settle you in tents, as in the days of old.
Or can a man walk upon burning coals and his feet not be scorched?
So it is with one who goes in to his fellow's wife to live with her: no one who draws near her will be acquitted.
One should not be bitter toward a thief who steals to satisfy himself because he is hungry.
I spoke with the prophets, and I multiplied prophecies; and through the prophets I sent messages.
If they were under compulsion in Gilead, nevertheless in Bais Gilgal they sacrificed oxen to idols. They also multiplied their shrines like heaps along the boundaries of a field.
The prophet said to them: Did not Jacob your father go to the fields of Aram? Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he guarded sheep.
And also, when your fathers went down to Egypt, יְיָ sent a prophet and brought Israel up from Egypt; and through a prophet Israel was protected.
Those of the house of Ephraim provoke anger and add further sin. The guilt of the innocent blood that he shed will return upon him, and his Master will return his reproach to him.
When one of the house of Ephraim spoke, trembling seized the nations; they were exalted in Israel. But now that they have sinned to the point of worshiping idols, they are being killed.
One who commits adultery with a woman lacks understanding; it is one who wishes to destroy his own life who does it.
He will encounter blows and disgrace, and his reproach will not be forgotten.
For jealousy is a husband's fury, and he will not have pity on the day of retribution.
He will show no favor to anyone who gives him a gift, and he will not be appeased when you increase the bribe.
My son, guard my word, and store up my commandments with you.
Guard my commandments and live, and guard my teachings like the pupil of your eye.
Therefore they will be like a morning cloud, like dew whose moisture comes to an end, like chaff that the wind blows from the threshing floor, and like smoke from a fire vent.
And I am יְיָ your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. You shall know no god apart from Me, and there is no deliverer except Me.
I supplied your needs in the wilderness, in a land where you were in need of everything.
When I fed them, they were filled to satiety, and their heart grew haughty; therefore they abandoned My worship.
Bind them upon your fingers; write them upon the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom, 'You are my sister,' and call understanding a kinswoman.
For I peered out through the small windows of my house, and through the openings of the dwelling.
He contended in might with an angel and prevailed; he wept and made entreaty of him. At Bais El he revealed himself to him, and there he will speak with us.

qualifications.he: המקור אינו מכנה בשם את הבוכה והמבקש. הכינויים נשמרים בלי לקבוע אם מדובר ביעקב המבקש מן המלאך או במלאך המבקש מיעקב.
qualifications.en: The source does not name the one who wept and entreated. The pronouns are retained without deciding between Jacob entreating the angel and the angel entreating Jacob.

qualifications.he: גם במשפט הגילוי בבית אל לא נוספו שמות לפועלים או למקבל הגילוי. הפסוק הבא מזכיר במפורש את ה׳ שנגלה לאבות; כאן נשמרים הכינויים עצמם, וכן המעבר מ'עליו' ל'עמנו' ולשון העתיד בדיבור.
qualifications.en: No names are added for the actors or recipient in the Bais El revelation clause. The following verse explicitly mentions God revealing Himself to the patriarchs; here the pronouns themselves are retained, together with the shift from 'to him' to 'with us' and the future expression of speaking.
qualifications.anchor: בְּבֵית אַל אִתְגְלֵי עֲלוֹהִי וְתַמָן יְמַלֵיל עִמָנָא

pairs.fullEnglish: And now they continue to sin, and have made themselves a cast image from their silver—idols in their own likeness, all of them the work of craftsmen. False prophets lead them astray: they sacrifice to the work of human hands; they slaughter oxen for calves.

qualifications.he: נביאי השקר הם המטעים. בפעלי ההקרבה והשחיטה נשמרת לשון רבים בלי לקבוע אם הכוונה במישרין לנביאים או למוטעים. נשמרו גם מושא ההקרבה, מעשה ידי אדם, והשוורים הנשחטים לעגלים; לא הוחלף אחד מן המושאים באנשים.
qualifications.en: The false prophets are the ones who mislead. The sacrificing and slaughtering verbs retain their plural reference without deciding whether they directly concern the prophets or those misled. Their objects are also retained: human handiwork as the recipient of sacrifice, and oxen slaughtered for calves; neither object has been replaced with people.
qualifications.anchor: לְהוֹן אִינוּן מַטְעָן נְבִיֵי שִׁקְרָא דָבְחִין לְעוֹבַד יְדֵי אֱנָשָׁא תּוֹרַיָא לְעֶגְלַיָא נָכְסִין

pairs.fullEnglish: For the matter of a prostitute is like a loaf of bread, but a man's wife hunts a precious life.

qualifications.he: 'מִלְתָא דְזַנְיָתָא' נמסר בלשון הכללית 'עניינה של זונה'. המקור מדמה אותו לכיכר לחם, אך אינו מפרש כאן אם מדובר במחיר, במפגש או בהתרוששות. התרגום משמר את ההשוואה בלי להוסיף הסבר כלכלי שאינו נאמר.
qualifications.en: 'מִלְתָא דְזַנְיָתָא' is rendered broadly as 'the matter of a prostitute.' The source compares it to a loaf of bread but does not specify here a fee, an encounter or impoverishment. The translation retains the comparison without adding an unstated economic explanation.
qualifications.anchor: מְטוּל דְדָמְיָא מִלְתָא דְזַנְיָתָא הֵיךְ גְרִצְתָּא דְלַחְמָא

pairs.fullEnglish: So that they may guard you from a woman who is an outsider, and from a foreign woman whose words are smooth.

qualifications.he: 'חִילוֹנִיתָא' נמסר במובן הכללי של אישה שמחוץ לחוגו של האדם, ולצדו נשמר בנפרד 'נוּכְרֵיתָא'. התרגום אינו קובע מן המילים הללו לבדן זהות דתית, מוצא מסוים או מעמד נישואין, ואינו טוען ששני הכינויים מציינים בהכרח שתי נשים שונות.
qualifications.en: 'חִילוֹנִיתָא' is rendered broadly as a woman who is an outsider, with 'נוּכְרֵיתָא' separately retained as 'foreign woman.' These words alone are not used to assign a religious identity, a particular origin or marital status, nor to claim that the two descriptions necessarily denote two different women.

pairs.fullEnglish: Those of the house of Ephraim have multiplied lies before Me, and those of the house of Israel have done so through their deceit. But those of the house of Judah remained steadfast in worship until the people of God were exiled from their land. Those who had been worshiping before Me in the Sanctuary are called a holy people; in this they remained steadfast.

qualifications.he: הסיום 'בְּכֵן הֲווֹ קַיָמִין' נקשר כאן באופן כללי לעבודה ולתיאור העם הקדוש שבמשפט הקודם. 'בכך עמדו' אינו קובע שנאמנותם נמשכה לאחר הגלות; המשפט הקודם מציין במפורש את הגלות כגבול תיאור העמידה בעבודה.
qualifications.en: The ending 'בְּכֵן הֲווֹ קַיָמִין' is linked broadly here to the preceding worship and description of a holy people. 'In this they remained steadfast' does not assert that their faithfulness continued after exile; the preceding sentence expressly describes steadfast worship up to exile.
qualifications.anchor: וְאִינוּן דַהֲווֹ פָלְחִין קָדָמַי בְּבֵית מַקְדָשָׁא מִתְקְרָן עַמָא קַדִישָׁא בְּכֵן הֲווֹ קַיָמִין

pairs.fullEnglish: Can a person put fire in his bosom (in his embrace) and his clothing not burn?

qualifications.he: החלופה שבסוגריים נשמרת: 'בחיקו (בחיבוקו)'. שתי הלשונות מובנות כאן בתחום החיק וההחזקה סמוך לגוף, בהתאם לנתינת האש ולשרפת הבגד שבהמשך. אין בכך שינוי של אותיות המקור או מחיקה של החלופה, ואין צורך לקרוא אותה כאן כ'בחטאיו'.
qualifications.en: The parenthetical alternative is retained as 'in his bosom (in his embrace).' Both expressions are understood here in the bodily sense of the bosom or holding close, matching the placement of fire and the ensuing burning of clothing. Neither source form is altered or deleted, and the alternative need not be read here as 'in his sins.'

pairs.fullEnglish: I looked among the children, considered the youths, and marveled at one lacking understanding.

qualifications.he: 'שַׁבְרֵי' ו'טְלָאֵי' נמסרים כאן בכינויים הכלליים 'ילדים' ו'צעירים'. אין בכך קביעת גיל מדויק או חלוקה לשתי קבוצות שאינן חופפות; כינויי הנעורים יכולים לשאת גם גוון של חוסר בשלות. התמיהה על חסר ההבנה שבסיום היא פעולה נפרדת ונשמרת בתרגום.
qualifications.en: 'שַׁבְרֵי' and 'טְלָאֵי' are rendered by the broad descriptions 'children' and 'youths.' This assigns neither exact ages nor two nonoverlapping groups; the youthful descriptions can also carry a shade of immaturity. The final marveling at one who lacks understanding is a separate action and is retained in the translation.

pairs.fullEnglish: Those of the house of Ephraim said: Indeed, we have become rich; we have gained power for ourselves. The prophet said to them: All your wealth will not endure for you on the day of repayment for your sins.

qualifications.he: אוֹנָס נמסר כאן במובן הרחב של כוח, על רקע לשון האונס והכפייה. הוא הדבר שהדוברים אומרים שהשיגו לעצמם, ולא תיאור מפורש של הדרך שבה רכשו רווח אחר. אין כאן קביעה אם הכוח הוא כלכלי, מדיני או כוח שנעשה בו שימוש במעשה מסוים.
qualifications.en: אוֹנָס is rendered here by the broad term 'power', with its force/coercion associations. It is what the speakers say they have gained for themselves, not an explicit description of the means by which they acquired a separate gain. The wording does not specify economic power, political power or its exercise in a particular act.

pairs.fullEnglish: Like a bird that comes openly, so will those who were exiled to the land of Egypt come; and like a dove that settles inside its nesting place, so will those who were driven away to the land of Assyria return. I will settle them peacefully in their homes, and My Word will be their support, says יְיָ.

qualifications.he: בִגְלֵי מתאר כאן ביאה בגלוי, והוא מתורגם openly. אין בצירוף קביעה של מהירות או של ביאה בלהקות. אין לערבב אותו עם דִגְלוֹ שבהמשך, המציין את מי שגלו למצרים. גם השלום נאמר במפורש בהמשך על ההשבה לבתים, ואין להוסיפו כתיאור נפרד של מעוף הציפור.
qualifications.en: בִגְלֵי describes coming openly and is rendered 'openly.' The expression does not specify speed or arrival in flocks. It is distinct from the following דִגְלוֹ, which identifies those exiled to Egypt. Peace is expressly stated later of resettlement in their homes and is not added as a separate description of the bird's flight.

pairs.fullEnglish: As you walk, it will accompany you; as you lie down, it will keep watch over you; and when you awake, it will be your advocate.

qualifications.he: רָצְיָךְ נקרא כאן כתיאור מי שמבקש או מליץ בעדך, מן המשמעות של ריצוי ובקשת רצון, ולא כמתן עצה או כשיחה בלבד. המבנה הִיא תֶהֱוֵי מציג תפקיד זה כנשוא; לכן נבחר 'מי שמליץ בעדך' באנגלית. רש״י מפרש את תשיחך שבעברית 'תָּלִיץ בַּעֲדֶךָ', התאמה עניינית שאינה ציטוט מפורש שלו ללשון התרגום. אין תוספת של קבר, תחיית המתים או מעמד דין; ההליכה, השכיבה והיקיצה נשארות ככתוב, וגם הכינוי נשמר בלי שם נוסף.
qualifications.en: רָצְיָךְ is read here as the one pleading on your behalf, in the propitiatory/intercessory sense, rather than merely giving advice or conversing. הִיא תֶהֱוֵי predicates that role, hence 'your advocate.' Rashi explains the Hebrew תשיחך as 'תָּלִיץ בַּעֲדֶךָ,' a close contextual parallel but not an explicit quotation by him of the Targum. No grave, resurrection or judgment scene is added; walking, lying down and awakening remain as stated, and the pronoun is preserved without a new name.

pairs.fullEnglish: But when he is found, he pays seven for one and gives his household's entire fortune.

qualifications.he: מַזָלָא מציינת מזל או גורל, וכאן fortune שומרת על המובן הרחב של מזלו או שגשוגו של הבית. בתרגום משלי יג:יא אותה מילה מתוארת כדבר הפוחת אצל בעליו, ובהמשך נזכר ממונו של הנותן לעני; וביט:ד היא מרבה חברים בניגוד למצבו של העני. ההקשרים האלה נותנים כאן מקום למשמעות כלכלית של שגשוג, בלי להפוך את המילה לשם של סוג נכס מוגדר. כּוּלֵיהּ מציין את הכול, דְבַיְתֵיהּ קושר את הדבר לביתו, ויָהֵיב אומר שהוא נותן אותו. הנתינה באה לצד תשלום של שבעה תמורת אחד. אין כאן פירוט של כסף, קרקע או רכוש אחר, ואין הכרח לקרוא זאת כקביעה אסטרולוגית; גם אין מחליפים את מַזָלָא במילה אחרת. המילה האנגלית fortune אינה כשלעצמה ראיה שהשם הארמי פירושו הון.
qualifications.en: מַזָלָא denotes fortune or lot; here fortune retains the broad sense of the household's fortune or prosperity. In this Targum's Proverbs 13:11 the same word describes something that diminishes for its owner, followed by a reference to the money of one who gives to the poor; in 19:4 it brings more friends, in contrast to the poor person's condition. These contexts allow an economic force of prosperity here without turning the noun into the name of a particular kind of asset. כּוּלֵיהּ expresses entirety, דְבַיְתֵיהּ attaches it to his household, and יָהֵיב says that he gives it. This giving accompanies payment of seven for one. No money, land or other property is itemized, no astrological assertion is required, and מַזָלָא is not replaced with another word. The English word fortune does not by itself prove that the Aramaic noun means wealth.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yaakov told Rachel that he was the son of her father's brother and that he was Rivkah's son; and she ran and told her father.

qualifications.he: התרגום מוסר את הקריאה המילולית של בַר אֲחָה דְאָבוּהָ: בן אחי אביה. אין זה הניסוח ׳בן אחות אביה׳. לצד זאת נאמר כאן שיעקב בן רבקה; בפסוק י לבן הוא אחי אמו, ובפסוק יג יעקב נקרא בן אחות לבן. ההבדל בין ביטויי הקרבה נשאר גלוי, ואין מן המשפט הזה לבדו קביעה חדשה על אביו של יעקב. אין מחליפים את אֲחָה באֲחָתֵיהּ או מעלימים את רכיב הבן שבבַר.
qualifications.en: The translation gives the literal reading of בַר אֲחָה דְאָבוּהָ: 'son of her father's brother'. This is not the wording 'son of her father's sister'. Alongside it, this verse calls Yaakov Rivkah's son; verse 10 makes Lavan his mother's brother, and verse 13 calls Yaakov Lavan's sister's son. The difference between these kinship expressions remains visible, and this sentence alone is not made into a new determination about Yaakov's father. אֲחָה is not replaced with אֲחָתֵיהּ, and the son component of בַר is not suppressed.

pairs.fullEnglish: I will not carry out the full force of My anger, nor will My Word again destroy the house of Israel. For I am God; My Word endures forever, and My deeds are not like the deeds of flesh who dwell upon the earth. Thus I have decreed by My Word that My holy Divine Presence shall be among you, and I will not again exchange Jerusalem for another city.

qualifications.he: קִרְוָא היא כאן שם עצם בנקבה יחידה, במשמעות עיר או יישוב; במילון יאסטרוב הצורה המדויקת מובאת במשמעות זו תוך הפניה לפסוק הזה, וצורות הרבים נמנות בנפרד. אוֹחֲרֵי יכולה לתאר שם עצם ביחיד, ואין להסיק רבים מן היו״ד שבסופה. משמעות הצירוף היא אפוא ״בעיר אחרת״. ירושלים היא הדבר שאין מחליפים, הבי״ת מציינת את החלופה, ועוד פירושה שוב. זהו תיאור אי־החלפת ירושלים, בהמשך להשראת השכינה בקרב העם; אין מחליפים אותו בפירוש של שנאה ללשון הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: Here קִרְוָא is a feminine singular noun meaning a city or settlement. Jastrow gives this exact form with the town/village meaning, cites this verse, and lists the plural forms separately. אוֹחֲרֵי can modify a singular noun; its final yod does not establish a plural. The expression therefore means 'for another city'. Jerusalem is what is not exchanged, the בְּ phrase gives the alternative, and עוֹד means 'again'. This is the city-exchange statement following the holy Divine Presence among the people; a hatred interpretation of the Hebrew verse is not substituted for it.
qualifications.anchor: וְלָא אֲחַלֵיף בְּקִרְוָא אוֹחֲרֵי עוֹד יְרוּשְׁלֵם

dayTitle.en: The Ladder and the Promise of Protection

explanation.he: יעקב יוצא לחרן ולן בדרך, ובחלומו הוא רואה סולם ומלאכים. אונקלוס מתאר את כבוד ה׳ העומד עליו ואת מימרו התומך בו, לצד הבטחות הארץ, ריבוי הבנים והשיבה.
explanation.en: Yaakov leaves for Charan and spends the night on the way, where he dreams of a ladder and angels. Onkelos describes the glory of יְיָ standing over him and His Word supporting him, together with the promises of land, numerous descendants, and return.

dayTitle.en: A Place of Favor and a Gate Facing Heaven

explanation.he: בהתעוררו יעקב מכיר בכך שכבוד ה׳ שורה במקום שלא ידע את מעלתו. אונקלוס מדגיש שאין זה מקום הדיוט אלא מקום רצון, ויעקב מציב בו אבן וקורא לו בית אל.
explanation.en: On awakening, Yaakov recognizes that the glory of יְיָ dwells in a place whose distinction he had not known. Onkelos emphasizes that it is no ordinary place but a place of Divine favor, and Yaakov sets up a stone there and names it Bais El.

dayTitle.en: Yaakov's Vow and the Well in the Field

explanation.he: יעקב קושר את נדרו לשמירה בדרך, למזון וללבוש ולשיבה בשלום לבית אביו. הוא מתחייב לעבוד לפני ה׳ על האבן ולהפריש מעשר, ואחר כך ממשיך מזרחה ומגיע לבאר.
explanation.en: Yaakov frames his vow around protection on the journey, food and clothing, and a peaceful return to his father's house. He undertakes to worship before יְיָ upon the stone and to set apart a tenth, then continues eastward and reaches a well.

dayTitle.en: The Shepherds Wait for the Stone to Be Removed

explanation.he: ליד הבאר יעקב שואל את הרועים על מוצאם ועל שלומו של לבן, והם מצביעים על רחל המתקרבת. הצעתו להשקות את הצאן ולחזור למרעה נענית בהסבר שצריך להמתין לכינוס כל העדרים ולהסרת האבן.
explanation.en: At the well, Yaakov asks the shepherds where they come from and whether Lavan is well, and they point out Rachel approaching. His proposal to water the sheep and return to pasture meets their explanation that they must wait for all the flocks to gather and for the stone to be removed.

dayTitle.en: Rachel and Yaakov Meet at the Well

explanation.he: יעקב מסיר את האבן ומשקה את צאן לבן כאשר הוא רואה את רחל, בת אחי אמו. הוא מספר לרחל שהוא בן רבקה, והיא רצה לספר לאביה. לבן יוצא לקראת יעקב, בן אחותו, מקבל אותו לביתו ושומע ממנו את סיפורו.
explanation.en: Yaakov removes the stone and waters Lavan's flock when he sees Rachel, the daughter of his mother's brother. He tells Rachel that he is Rivkah's son, and she runs to tell her father. Lavan goes out to meet Yaakov, his sister's son, welcomes him into his house, and hears his account.

dayTitle.en: Yaakov's Marriages and the Building of the Family

explanation.he: עבודתו של יעקב בעבור רחל מובילה להחלפתה בלאה ולנישואיו לשתיהן, תוך התחייבות לשנות עבודה נוספות. אונקלוס מתאר את יפי עיני לאה ואת ההיריון שניתן לה, ומביא את דבריה בכל לידת בן. מול כאבה של רחל יעקב מפנה את הבקשה אל ה׳, והיא מוסרת לו את בלהה ומתחייבת לגדל את ילדיה.
explanation.en: Yaakov's service for Rachel leads to Leah being substituted for her and to his marrying both, with a commitment to further years of work. Onkelos describes the beauty of Leah's eyes and the conception granted to her, and records her words at each son's birth. In response to Rachel's distress, Yaakov directs her request to יְיָ, and she gives him Bilhah and undertakes to raise her children.

dayTitle.he: המשפחה גדלה ויעקב יוצא לשוב לארצו
dayTitle.en: The Family Grows and Yaakov Sets Out to Return to His Land

explanation.he: לידות הבנים נמסרות לצד קבלת תפילותיהן של רחל ולאה, ולאחר לידת יוסף יעקב מבקש לשוב לארצו. הסכם השכר בצאן מביא לריבוי נכסיו ולמתיחות עם בית לבן, ואז מצטווה יעקב לשוב בהבטחת סיוע מימרו של ה׳. המרדף מסתיים בתוכחת יעקב על שנות עבודתו ובברית שהגל והמצבה מעידים עליה. לאחר פרידת לבן, יעקב ממשיך בדרכו ופוגש מלאכים.
explanation.en: The sons' births are related alongside the acceptance of Rachel's and Leah's prayers, and after Yosef's birth Yaakov asks to return to his land. The livestock wage agreement brings increasing property and tension with Lavan's household, after which Yaakov is commanded to return with the promise of support from the Word of יְיָ. The pursuit ends with Yaakov's rebuke concerning his years of service and a covenant witnessed by the heap and pillar. After Lavan leaves, Yaakov continues on his way and encounters angels.

dayTitle.en: Mercy, the Gathering of Exiles, and Steadfast Worship

explanation.he: תרגום הושע מתאר עם הנחלק על השיבה לדרכי ה׳, ומולו רחמים המתעוררים וזכירת הברית. הוא מדגיש את קיום המאמר, את השכינה הקדושה בתוך העם ואת השבת הגולים לבתיהם בשלום. הסיום מבחין בין הכזב והמרמה של אפרים וישראל לבין עמידת בית יהודה בעבודה במקדש.
explanation.en: The Targum of Hoshea describes a people divided about returning to God's ways, set against awakened mercy and the word of the covenant. It emphasizes the enduring Divine Word, the holy Divine Presence among the people, and the exiles' peaceful return to their homes. The ending contrasts the lies and deceit of Ephraim and Israel with the house of Judah's steadfast worship in the Sanctuary.

dayTitle.he: מן המרמה והריב אל שמירת הוראת ההורים
dayTitle.en: From Deceit and Strife to Guarding Parental Teaching

explanation.he: הקריאה מונה גאווה, שקר, שפיכות דם, מחשבות רעות והטלת מריבה בין אחים. אחר כך היא פונה אל הבן לשמור את מצוות אביו ואת הוראת אמו ולקשור אותן ללבו. ההוראה מתוארת כמלווה את הליכתו ושומרת עליו בשכבו, ונוכחת עמו גם ביקיצתו.
explanation.en: The reading lists pride, falsehood, bloodshed, evil thoughts, and the setting of quarrels between brothers. It then addresses the son, urging him to guard his father's commandment and his mother's teaching and to bind them within his heart. That teaching accompanies his walking, watches over his lying down, and remains with him upon waking.

dayTitle.en: False Alliances and the Recollection of Jacob's Strength

explanation.he: תרגום הושע מדמה את ישראל לזורע רוח וקוצר סערה, ומפרט כזב, ביזה ובריתות עם אשור ומצרים. מול החשבון על המעשים, הנביא מזכיר את גדולת יעקב שנאמרה עוד לפני לידתו ואת התמודדותו עם המלאך. הקריאה מסתיימת בבכי ובבקשה, בגילוי בבית אל ובדיבור המופנה גם אל 'עמנו'.
explanation.en: The Targum of Hoshea likens Israel to one who sows wind and reaps a whirlwind, specifying lies, plunder, and dealings with Assyria and Egypt. Alongside the accounting for deeds, the prophet recalls Jacob's promised greatness before his birth and his struggle with the angel. The reading ends with weeping and entreaty, revelation at Bais El, and speech extending to 'us.'

dayTitle.en: The Commandment's Light and Protection from Seduction

explanation.he: התרגום מתאר את המצווה כנר ואת ההוראה כאור, וקושר את דרך החיים לתוכחה ולמשמעת. כנגד לשון חלקה ויופי מפתה הוא מזהיר שלא לחמוד בלב ושלא להילכד. סיום הקריאה מעמיד את דימוי כיכר הלחם מול ציד הנפש היקרה בידי אשת איש.
explanation.en: The Targum describes the commandment as a lamp and teaching as light, connecting the way of life with reproof and discipline. Against smooth speech and alluring beauty, it warns against inward desire and entrapment. The ending sets the image of a loaf of bread against a married woman's hunting of a precious life.

dayTitle.en: Kindness and Justice in Place of Deceptive Balances

explanation.he: הנביא מזכיר את האל שנגלה לאבות ואת זכרו לדור ודור, ומורה להתחזק בעבודתו ולשמור חסד ומשפט. תרגום הושע מזהיר מפני מסחר במאזני מרמה ומעמיד מול התפארות אפרים בעושרו את יום תשלום החטאים. לבסוף נשמעת הבטחת האל שהוציא ממצרים להושיב שוב באוהלים כימי קדם.
explanation.en: The prophet recalls the God revealed to the patriarchs and His memorial through every generation, calling for steadfast worship, kindness, and justice. The Targum of Hoshea warns against trade with deceptive balances and sets the day of repayment for sins against Ephraim's boast of wealth. It ends with the promise of the God who brought Israel out of Egypt to settle them again in tents as in former days.

dayTitle.en: The Prophets' Mission against Increasing Sin

explanation.he: תרגום הושע מזכיר דיבור ושליחות באמצעות הנביאים, ומעמיד מולם הקרבת שוורים לאלילים וריבוי מקומות פולחן. הוא שב אל יעקב, אבי העם, ששמר צאן בעבור אישה, ואל הנביא שבאמצעותו הועלה ישראל ממצרים ונשמר. סיום הקריאה מתאר את החטא הנוסף, את חזרת אשמת הדם ואת המעבר מגדולת אפרים להריגתו בעקבות עבודת האלילים.
explanation.en: The Targum of Hoshea recalls speech and messages through the prophets, set against the sacrifice of oxen to idols and the multiplication of shrines. It returns to Jacob, the people's father, who guarded sheep for a wife, and to the prophet through whom Israel was brought up from Egypt and protected. The ending describes further sin, returning bloodguilt, and Ephraim's passage from eminence to being killed after turning to idolatry.

dayTitle.he: חורבן הניאוף ושמירת ההוראה כבבת העין
dayTitle.en: Adultery's Ruin and Guarding Teaching like the Eye's Pupil

explanation.he: התרגום מתאר ניאוף כמעשה של חסר הבנה המביא חבלה בנפש, מכות ובושה. קנאת הבעל מוצגת כחמה שאינה מתפייסת במתנות או בריבוי שוחד. משם הקריאה עוברת לפנייה אל הבן לשמור את המאמר ואת המצוות, ולנצור את ההוראות כבבת העין.
explanation.en: The Targum describes adultery as an act of deficient understanding that brings self-destruction, blows, and disgrace. The husband's jealousy is presented as fury that cannot be appeased by gifts or increased bribery. The reading then turns to the son, calling him to guard the word and the commandments and to protect the teachings like the pupil of his eye.

dayTitle.en: Silver Calves and Forsaking the Provider in the Wilderness

explanation.he: תרגום הושע מתאר צלמים העשויים מכסף ומעשה אומנים, הטעיה בידי נביאי שקר ושחיטת שוורים לעגלים. כנגדם הוא מציג את האל שהעלה ממצרים וסיפק את צורכי העם במדבר, ואת שלילת קיומו של גואל אחר. הסיום קושר את השובע ואת גבהות הלב לעזיבת עבודתו.
explanation.en: The Targum of Hoshea describes silver idols made by craftsmen, deception by false prophets, and the slaughter of oxen for calves. Against them it presents the God who brought Israel up from Egypt and supplied the people's needs in the wilderness, denying that there is any other deliverer. The ending connects satiety and a haughty heart with the abandonment of His worship.

dayTitle.he: קרבת החכמה ומבט אל חסר ההבנה
dayTitle.en: Wisdom as Kin and a View of One Lacking Understanding

explanation.he: הקריאה מצווה לקשור את ההוראות לאצבעות ולכתוב אותן על לוח הלב. החכמה נקראת אחות והבינה קרובת משפחה, כנגד האישה הזרה שדבריה חלקים. אחר כך הדובר מתאר מבט מחלונות ביתו אל הצעירים ותמיהה על חסר הבנה.
explanation.en: The reading calls for binding the teachings upon the fingers and writing them on the heart's tablet. Wisdom is addressed as a sister and understanding as a kinswoman, in contrast with the foreign woman whose words are smooth. The speaker then describes looking from his house's windows toward the young and marveling at one who lacks understanding.

dayTitle.en: Fire, Adultery, and Repayment for Theft

explanation.he: הקריאה שואלת אם אפשר לשאת אש או ללכת על גחלים בלי להיכוות, ומשווה לכך את הקרבה לאשת הזולת. לאחר מכן היא מזכירה גנב הפועל מתוך רעב, אך אינה משמיטה את התשלום כשהוא נמצא. התרגום מציין במפורש תשלום של שבעה תחת אחד.
explanation.en: The reading asks whether one can carry fire or walk on coals without being burned, and compares this with approaching another man's wife. It then mentions a thief acting from hunger, without omitting repayment when he is found. The Targum explicitly specifies repayment of seven for one.
